title: Always show all categories, even if empty

comments.body:
Thanks for your feedback, however this is an engine limitation. You have two options here: 

1. statically say which items the menu has
2. make the answer return the facet, even if it has 0 results

The second option would be the preferable for you, but it's not possible. I did put it on our internal feedback board. 

duplicate of https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-client-javascript/issues/541

To complete @Haroenv's answer, the second option can be emulated using a first empty query. In order to do this you need to [create a custom widget](https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/v2/guides/custom-widget.html).

During the init, you should use the helper to make a new query using [searchOnce](https://community.algolia.com/algoliasearch-helper-js/reference.html#AlgoliaSearchHelper#searchOnce) and with the answer build your menu items. The facet values that you retrieve then can be used for filtering, with [helper.toggleFacetRefinement](https://community.algolia.com/algoliasearch-helper-js/reference.html#AlgoliaSearchHelper#toggleFacetRefinement).

The idea is that since you want a static menu, you shouldn't need to rerender anything afterwards.

As a side note, for implementation issues, we recommend using [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/tags/instantsearch.js/) or our [community forum](https://discourse.algolia.com/). This helps keep the issues for bugs or feature proposals, which really helps us :)

For reference, we'll soon document a user-land solution for this leveraging `transformItems` on the "[Customize an Existing Widget](https://www.algolia.com/doc/guides/building-search-ui/widgets/customize-an-existing-widget/js)" page. This workaround will look like [this example](https://codesandbox.io/s/instantsearchjs-facets-with-count-of-0-pk62m).
